Below are objects in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, listed by title only.
For each one, give what you know about that specific object:
- "artist": the artist or maker, or "unknown" if anonymous or you don't know
- "year": the year it was made, as one integer (negative for BCE), your best estimate
- "medium": its medium or material, briefly
- "familiarity": how well you know this specific object, from 0 (never heard of it) to 1 (know it well)

Reply with only a JSON array, one object per item, each with "id", "artist", "year", "medium", "familiarity".

127. On the Way to Coney Island

129. Embossed Plan of the City of New York
130. Musketeer Galloping Towards the Left
131. Phylloptera oblongifolia

133. Chinese Chairs, in Chippendale Drawings, Vol. I
134. Old Farmhouse

136. Quoits, from the Games and Sports series (N165) for Old Judge Cigarettes
137. Glasscock, Shortstop, Indianapolis, from the Old Judge series (N172) for Gypsy Queen and Old Judge Cigarettes
138. The Pyramid of Gaius Cestius, from "Vedute di Roma" (Roman Views), part II
139. On fait des conts à l'actionnaire, from Les Lorettes, plate 7
140. Le Lundi, from Physionomies Parisiennes, Masques et Visages, plate 43
141. Colossal statue of the Appenino by Giambologna to left, represented as a giant crouching at the entrance of a grotto, ramps to either side, a pond below, various figures, dogs, and birds to right, from 'Views of the villa at Pratolino' (Vues de la villa de Pratolino)
142. Leslie Chester, from the Actors and Actresses series (N45, Type 1) for Virginia Brights Cigarettes
143. Venus, from 'Game of Mythology' (Jeu de la Mythologie)
144. Sixth scene, the heavens, from 'The marriage of the gods' (Le nozze degli Dei)
145. Pulliciniello and Signora Lucretia, from Balli di Sfessania (Dance of Sfessania), plate 9
146. Portrait of Claude Deruet and His Son, Jean
147. Iris: Sweet Message, from the series Floral Beauties and Language of Flowers (N75) for Duke brand cigarettes
148. Horizontal Frieze with a Pattern of Decorative Fern Leaves on Background of Horizontal Stripes
149. Medea Calls on the Gods' Aid, from Les Metamorphoses d'Ovide, Traduction nouvelle Avec le texte latin, suivie d'une analyse de l'explication des Fables, de notes géographiques, historiques, mythologiques et critiques, Par M.G.T. Villenave; ornée de gravures d'après les dessins de MM. LeBarbier, Monsiau et Moreau. A Paris, Chez les Éditeurs, F. Gay Libraire, rue de la Harpe, Bureau de la Bible; Ch. Guestard, Avocat, rue Saint Germain-l'Auxerrois. De l'Imprimerie de P. Didot l'aîné. MDCCCVI.
150. Proof for White Line Square series
